key_insight: A 3D physics-informed neural network couples patient-specific pulmonary blood flow with Windkessel outlet models by separating basal pressure from small spatial pressure variations.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a meshless complement to CFD for patient-specific hemodynamics and estimation of distal vascular parameters.
method: Embed blood-flow equations and dynamic Windkessel RCR outlet conditions in PINN training.
Separate basal and spatial pressure, with a Windkessel initial condition, pressure gauge, and global mass-balance constraint.
Use periodic Fourier time embedding to represent pulsatile flow.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D channels and a patient-specific right pulmonary artery reproduced flow and pressure at errors on the order of data resolution; inverse estimation recovered three Windkessel parameters from synthetic data with about 0.3% error.
watch_item: Residual local-pressure biases remain, and robustness to noisy clinical data has not yet been established.
paper_title: A 3D PINN-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
